quest.title: The Man Who Once Lied
quest.description: Nefer seems to have issued a certain commission at the Adventurers' Guild...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3, The Man Who Became a Mule x1

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: Here you go, Lady Nefer — the book you were looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let me see... Ha, would you look at that? Finally, an actual copy of "The Man Who Became a Mule."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that... Nefer? Surely she can't be here for a commission?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Nefer doesn't seem like the kind of person who "takes" commissions... More like the kind who dishes them out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, if you start taking work from Nefer, there'll be none left for Jahoda...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, what sort of job is Nefer delegating to the Adventurers' Guild? Paimon's kinda curious...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Not bad... This is exactly what I was looking for. The Adventurers' Guild must have quite the impressive network, tracking down a long-lost story like this...

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Haha, well, that's all thanks to our hardworking adventurers.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: There were quite a few setbacks along the way, but in the end, we managed to find a collector in Snezhnaya who had a copy.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: How ironic that a story about the desert would end up somewhere like Snezhnaya...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well, thank you for your efforts. I'll send over the payment as promised.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Also, Mr. Sarin — please keep this commission active, and raise its priority level. I'll cover the additional fee as well.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Not a problem. It's our honor to do business with you, Lady Nefer. If you'll excuse me, I'll go get everything sorted.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: My business is done, you two. You can come out and ask your questions. I know you're "curious"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You even heard what Paimon said!? Huh. Guess that's what makes you the boss...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, you're posting a commission?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Something like that. It's more like a long-term partnership I have with the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Come, let's head back to the Curatorium for a cup of tea. This isn't the best place for sharing stories...

choices.text: Better not bother Nefer right now.
Maybe I should have her give me some easy ones.

talks.objective: Return to the Curatorium of Secrets with Nefer

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Huh, looks like Jahoda's not back yet.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Wait here. I'll go brew some tea.

dialogues.speaker: Ashru
dialogues.text: Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here, kitty kitty...

dialogues.speaker: Ashru
dialogues.text: Meow, meow meow!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, who's a good kitty... C'mon, shake!

dialogues.speaker: Ashru
dialogues.text: Meow?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Alright, help yourselves. Cream and sugar is over there if you need it.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Looks like Ashru's taken a real liking to you. Back when I first brought him home, he was as fierce as a little lion.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: He didn't let anyone get close except for me. Anybody else who tried would have his little fangs and claws to contend with...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously? You'd never guess he used to be aggressive...

dialogues.speaker: Ashru
dialogues.text: Meow, meow meow? Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That was a long time ago, when the two of us had just arrived in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Back then, we had no one to rely on but ourselves. And to survive in a place like Nod-Krai... We had no choice but to bare our claws and teeth.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Of course, things are different now.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Anyway, it's about time we satisfied that curiosity of yours. I'm guessing you want to know more about my "long-term partnership" with the Adventurers' Guild?

choices.text: I still can't believe you would need to post a commission...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean like, some kind of extra special treasure even Nefer can't get her hands on?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: It's special, no doubt about that. But whether it counts as "treasure"... Well, that depends on how you see it.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Here, this is the book I asked the Adventurers' Guild to find for me. Take a look.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it's like a... fairytale from Sumeru!

choices.text: Is it a clue to finding hidden treasure?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh oh, not another riddle-filled treasure hunt! Well, uh... have fun! Paimon's gonna sit this one out...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Relax, it's just a story passed down among the desert-dwellers of Sumeru. There's no secret treasure, and no hidden riddles.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The only reason I went to such lengths to find it... is because it has to do with my father.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your father...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: That's right. From what you've seen before... you no doubt remember the fate that befell us.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Before he brought back those so-called "spoils of war," before our little village ended up buried under the desert sands... He used to tell me stories.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: You know what Sumeru was like back then. Tales like these, stories full of wisdom and warmth, were something only the lucky few living in the rainforests got to hear.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: But for the desert-dwellers, cut off from "civilization" by the Wall of Samiel... wisdom and warmth were luxuries we couldn't afford.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The stories passed down in the desert had one purpose, and one alone — to teach children how to survive.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: In desert tales, people who waste food get turned into scorpions, those who waste water end up losing their tongues...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The stories taught us to be kind, but to be scarce with our trust... to lie and deceive, as long as we didn't get caught.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: But, I suppose my father didn't want me to turn out like everyone else.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: He would take these stories and change them... imbue them with more... warmth.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: In the versions he told, liars turned into mules, killers fell off cliffs... But, picky children... ended up with a toothache, at most.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon kinda gets where he was coming from. After all, who doesn't wanna see their kids grow up with the right values...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, what did you think of those stories, Nefer?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Me?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I couldn't get enough of them. I'd spend my days counting down the minutes to nightfall, when Dad would lull me to sleep with another one of his stories.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Then, come daytime, I'd grab his storybook and go tell them to the other kids.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: They were so envious of me. No matter where I went, there was always a line of kids trailing behind me. They would do whatever I asked, just for the chance to hear a story.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And then, one day, it all came to an end, and now, all that remains of those times is buried under the sand. My father, my friends, my tribe... and all those stories, too.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: After that, I went to the Akademiya. It was there that I first discovered the "original versions" of some of his stories.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: In those versions, the liars were never punished, the murderers walked free... After all, if you fall for a lie, you deserve to be deceived. If the blade is in your hand, you get to write the rules...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And picky children? They ended up just like the ones who wasted water — turned into lizards, doomed to spend the rest of their days crawling under the rocks.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Only then did I realize that it was my father who'd been "deceiving" me all along, weaving a false world of warmth to shelter me from the harsh realities of the world.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: But once my father was gone, that world collapsed with him, and I had no choice but to face the truth.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Luckily, though, I was a quick learner. Before long, I'd turned into exactly the kind of "desert-dweller" he'd worked so hard to keep me from becoming.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: After that, it was all lies, deceit, revenge, and ruin — themes that have played out in the desert a thousand times over. But I'm sure you know that all too well.

choices.text: So the reason you started collecting these stories...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: More or less. I just want to know exactly how many lies a father might tell his own daughter.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: As the only person in this world he ever deceived so completely, I suppose I owe it to him to make an equally comprehensive record of his distortions. Besides, anonymity seems a cruel fate for such a prolific twister of the truth.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Anyway... Hmph, I'm sure Thoth, the Ibis King, would approve of what I'm doing.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: After all, he was the one who sent me in search of something that could "discern truth from falsehood."

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: When I was young, the stories my father told me shaped my understanding of the world.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Whereas their original endings... Heh, well, they taught me what this world is really like.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And it's true — for me, they really did help me "discern truth from falsehood."

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I figured that gathering them up might be the key to finding the answer the Ibis King was looking for.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: So, after I established myself in Nod-Krai, I started using every available channel to track down the stories my father once told me.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The problem was, nearly all of them were folk tales, parables passed down in the desert through word of mouth. Very few were ever written down.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: But living all the way out here in Nod-Krai, it wasn't like I could just go wandering around the desert to find those who still remembered them.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: As for Jahoda... Well, I was short on manpower as it was, so I needed a different plan.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And, considering the countless adventurers at their disposal, I decided to strike up a long-term partnership with the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: They bring me stories passed down among the desert people, I pay them accordingly, and sometimes, even do them a little favor in return.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Mr. Sarin was more than happy with my terms, so we soon came to an understanding. And from the way things have been going, I'd say our arrangement has worked out rather well.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So... What's special about the story you just got your hands on?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Ah, well... This was the very last story my father ever told me — the only one whose ending he left unchanged.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: A man who spent his life distorting the truth... Buried under the desert sand the one time he chose not to lie.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Hah... and look, it even says: "Deep down, his was a heart of gold — and that is the greatest wisdom of all." How ironic is that?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Anyway, I can make a copy of this story if you're interested.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: #Ah, and I just realized... You're an adventurer too, aren't you, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well, being an adventurer means you've traveled far and wide and seen many things...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I was just thinking... We could sign an agreement for a long-term partnership of our own.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: If you ever come across any stories about the desert-dwellers of Sumeru, bring them to me, and I'll make it worth your while.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, was that your goal this whole time? Just to ask us that?

choices.text: So, there was a commission at the end of this, after all...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Wonderful! Then, here's to a long and fruitful partnership.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And speaking of partnerships... Why isn't Jahoda back yet?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Was that job I gave her really that difficult?

choices.text: Well, taking commissions is what I do, so... Okay!
Was to find out what the originals were really like?
Is there some kind of riddle hidden inside?
It must be for something really important.
